questions.q: What is the main data-architecture benefit of a single-org strategy?
options: Every user automatically gets a free license
One shared data model and one place to report from across the whole business
Governor limits no longer apply
Master data is automatically synced from external systems
questions.explain: A single org means one copy of the schema and one copy of the data, so cross-business reporting is a single query instead of a cross-org integration project.

questions.q: A regulated subsidiary must keep customer data physically within its country's borders. What kind of requirement is this, and how does it typically affect org strategy?
options: A licensing requirement that has no effect on org strategy
A performance requirement solved by adding more storage to the existing org
A data residency requirement, which often pushes toward a separate org for that subsidiary
A governor-limit requirement solved by reducing SOQL query volume
questions.explain: Data residency law requiring data to stay within a specific country's infrastructure is a common, legitimate driver toward running a separate org for that subsidiary rather than a single global org.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine data cost of running multiple orgs instead of one?
options: Master data like customers and products now exists in more than one place with nothing keeping the copies in sync automatically
Apex governor limits become stricter in every org
Standard objects can no longer be customized
Reports can span multiple orgs natively with no integration needed
questions.explain: Multiple orgs mean multiple copies of master data with no built-in synchronization — this is exactly the cost a single org avoids, and it has to be solved with integration or MDM if multiple orgs are chosen.

questions.q: Why might an acquired company be kept on its own separate Salesforce org for a transition period rather than merged immediately?
options: Because Salesforce technically prevents merging two orgs under any circumstances
Because its existing mature implementation and data model may not map cleanly onto the parent's model yet, and forcing an immediate fit risks losing fidelity
Because separate orgs are always cheaper to license than one combined org
Because single orgs cannot contain more than one business unit's data
questions.explain: An acquired company's mature, divergent data model often needs a deliberate integration or migration plan rather than an immediate forced fit — keeping it separate temporarily protects data fidelity during that transition.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach to deciding between a single-org and multi-org strategy?
options: Always default to multi-org for large enterprises regardless of structure
Always default to single-org since it is categorically the safer choice
Lay out the specific tradeoffs against the business's actual structure, regulatory constraints, and growth plans, and revisit the decision periodically
Let each business unit decide independently with no central coordination
questions.explain: There is no universally correct default — the architect's job is to make the tradeoff explicit for this specific company's constraints and treat the decision as something to revisit as the business changes, not something decided once and forgotten.
